meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and why did he find out on his phone?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Go on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. I'm writing those down. Plenty of kids draft somewhere else and paste it in.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays quiet. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Turn it toward me. Seventeen-year-olds misremember Shakespeare all the time; a bad quotation is a mistake, not a verdict.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Then say what you're proposing, Hale.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay. And I asked what you're proposing.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, in writing, tonight. Owen does the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. And nobody in that class hears a word about it.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll check his shifts tonight. Put Thursday in the email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, after school, not in front of his class and before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require that confirmation in writing, with Thursday the twelfth after school as the date once I have checked his shifts, and an assurance that nobody in his class is told anything about this. I expect it in writing tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite, likely Thursday after school once she checks his shifts, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight that nothing goes on his record and his class hears nothing; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it with time to spare.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its times and then answered her paste-it-from-elsewhere defence by inviting a dated draft, which gave her something she could check rather than an opinion.
What cost ground: Very little; when she asked what you were proposing, you showed the outline instead, which read as a dodge and made her shorter and sharper for a turn.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, very close to that kind of night; that proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: The moment she asked what you were proposing, put 4.4 on the table straight away and keep the October 15 outline in reserve in case she pushed back on the rewrite.
